speaker: alse_pinder
text: I was out before four. The parish girls had the hedges, and my shoes are wet through.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Wet shoes are a May morning. How many boughs are in that apron.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Three. They gave me three. The lanes will have more, with ribbons. I have not been as far as the gate.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: The lanes are the parish's. This door is mine. One bough over the door, and no more.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: One. She was out before four. That is enough hawthorn for a lodging.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: May I put a second in the casement, Mistress.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: No second. One over the door, so the close can see we are not asleep, and not a twig more.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Leave it where she puts it. I am not improving your allowance.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Shall I tie it with ribbon. The girls had ribbon.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: No ribbon. The parish may dress a gate. A door is not a pole.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: No ribbon. One bough. No more.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: I will not bring a second in. The shoes I will dry on the stair.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: See that you do not. A custom is one bough. A wood is a different house. I do not keep a wood.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: If I come home to a wood, I shall believe the close and not you. I would rather believe you.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: You will find one. It will not be dressed up. Sunday may find it tired. That is a bough's business, not a May game.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Gib was on the book when I came down. The hawthorn is nothing to him.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Leave him on the second volume. I am going up to the gate before I eat, and the book is not coming with me.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Eat before you are witty on nothing. The loaf is short again, a finger and a half, and the price is still a penny.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will eat when I am back. I am not refusing a May morning.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Then eat a mouthful now. Threepence when you have eaten. I am not owed a comedy, and I am not owed a second bough.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: The thickest stem is on the hook. I will not move it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Leave it. One bough. I have the old man in my head on the way up, and the gate will not help him or hurt him.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Mind your purse at a gate on May morning. Where there are ribbons there are hands.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: My purse has the tables and a point. I am not carrying a sum to a maypole.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: If the girls are still at the arch, the hawthorn will be white on it. I saw it white in the hedges.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: The arch is not my door. Say the door back to me.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: One bough. No ribbon. No second.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: One bough. No more. I am going up. I will not bring the hedge home.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Then go. The board will be here when the gate is done with you.
